div.b: The helper caches with an expiry

div.span: - SETEX product:2 30 stores the value and its lifetime in one command, so staleness is bounded to 30 seconds by design.

div.span: - The helper repeats step 3 and caches again, which is how a read-through cache refreshes itself without an invalidation message.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 578px; height: 1px; padding-top: 697px; margin-left: 1060px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;

div.span: - Who reads: the helper, on the caller's behalf. The call site only ever asks for the key.
- Who writes the cache: the helper, after a miss, and always with a TTL.
- Hit vs miss: a hit is identical to cache-aside; a miss is what the TTL turns into a scheduled, predictable event instead of a surprise.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
